purpose: Declarations checked by .agent-harness/scripts/check_ssot_consistency.py. 'facts' are numbers that appear in prose and must agree across every surface: a fact is a value plus the commit it holds at, not a bare number, so a superseded value is legal exactly where it is dated. 'coverage_policy' names the claims that are excused from needing a statement in a live handoff region -- everything not named is required, so silence is never the permissive option. 'assertion_exemptions' names individual narrative lines in a LIVE region whose registry disagreement is corrected later in the same section; it is currently empty, because the one section that needed it -- '## Next action' in PROJECT_STATE.md -- is now marked superseded in its own heading, which is the better fix. Every entry here is re-verified on every run: a declaration that no longer describes the repository is an error, not a silent pass, so a dead exemption is reported rather than accumulating.

coverage_policy.note: Gates have no exemption list by design: every gate in GATE_REGISTRY.json must be asserted by name in a live region. Claims are different. Most registry claims are bounded findings sealed at their decision, whose status is carried by the FROZEN_DECISIONS.md row and the audit report that established them; forcing the rolling handoff to restate them would produce ceremonial prose rather than checkable prose. The claims NOT listed below are the ones the current handoff is actively carrying -- contested, critical-risk, or under live remediation -- and they must be stated where they are current. A claim added to CLAIM_REGISTRY.jsonl is required by default until someone writes down here why it is not.
